main_body: Tall rounded-top standing stone slab with cyan runes on its front face
top_band: Lighter grey-violet band at rows 7-10 with a rounded back edge, then an abrupt step to the darker front face from row 11
evidence: In the middle column, rows 7-10 are a light grey cap about 4 rows tall with a rounded outline. Row 11 is a dark shadow step, and below it the front face runs to about row 30 with a lighter left strip and a darker right strip. The cap is a real horizontal surface rather than a 1-2px rim, so it reads as a small 3/4 column cap. There is no separate front-edge highlight, and the runes are painted flat rather than inset. The top is thin but just acceptable.

style.evidence: The stone uses only about 3-4 grey steps, with a near-black, almost neutral outline all round, which gives the sticker look. The front face has large flat fills with no grain, chips or speckle. Apart from the runes, the tiles hold only a few colours each, well below the stall and well references, which carry tile scallops, per-stone shading and many colours per tile.
